title: US PCE nowcast – Broadening pressures lock in December rate hike
gist: Oxford Economics nowcasts US headline PCE inflation rising to 3.8% y/y in October from 3.6%, with high energy prices spilling into food and core, locking in a 25bp Fed hike in December; it thinks markets overprice a 50bp move. It expects headline inflation to peak in Q4 as oil falls and energy pass-through to core eases over 2027.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics nowcasts US headline PCE inflation rising to 3.8% y/y in October 2026, up from 3.6% y/y in September.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Hot inflation print ahead of FOMC; supportive of hawkish front-end pricing.

insights.claim: High US energy prices are lifting food inflation and bleeding into core PCE inflation, a broadening of price pressures that Oxford Economics says will discomfort the Federal Reserve.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Energy-to-core pass-through raises second-round inflation risk; watch core goods and food components.
insights.quote: high energy prices are lifting food inflation and bleeding into core inflation

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects a 25bp Federal Reserve rate hike at the December 2026 FOMC meeting, driven by broadening inflation pressures.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Positions for a hike in December; fade pure-pause scenarios in rates.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics believes markets are overpricing the odds of a 50bp Federal Reserve hike in December 2026, expecting only 25bp.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Potential trade: fade 50bp pricing in December fed funds futures / front-end.
insights.quote: we think markets are overpricing the odds of a 50bp hike

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts US headline inflation to peak in Q4 2026, helped by recent declines in oil prices.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A Q4 peak implies hiking cycle may be short; watch oil for confirmation.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects pass-through from higher energy prices to US core inflation to ease over 2027.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Supports a view that the Fed tightening will not need to extend deep into 2027.

insights.claim: Muted equity markets, lower demand for homebuying and modest wage growth should keep US services inflation benign, according to Oxford Economics.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Services disinflation channels limit core stickiness; weak equities/housing act as automatic brakes.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics replicates the BEA methodology monthly using CPI, PPI and import price data to estimate the PCE deflator, with average absolute errors of 3bps for both headline and core PCE.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A high-accuracy PCE nowcast lets traders front-run the official release once CPI/PPI print.

insights.claim: Almost all of Oxford Economics' PCE nowcast tracking error comes from core services ex-housing, where the share of confidential source data is largest.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Surprise risk in PCE vs. CPI/PPI-based estimates concentrates in core services ex-housing.
